_about: How people actually join Singapore Active Ageing Centres and what they get after joining - gathered from operator FAQ pages (THK, REACH, KWSH, PCF, TOUCH, Allkin, MWS) and MOH/PA (Nov 2026). This is the real join flow the Wisdom seed should mirror.

join_flow.what: Walk in or call the nearest centre
join_flow.detail: MWS: 'Walk to your nearest Active Ageing Centre and sign up for any activity or programme. Or call them to enquire.'
Age 60+, Singapore Citizen or PR, reside within the centre's service boundary (some centres accept neighbours regardless). Free of charge (KWSH states explicitly).
PCF: register your interest, the team shares activities, understands your interests, guides you through membership. Enrolment subject to vacancies.
Family, hospital discharge, or a community partner refers; the centre follows up (KWSH 'Social Connector' registers seniors for prescribed Healthier SG activities).
Drop in for whatever is on that day; book recurring classes; choose interest groups at your own comfort level ('We welcome seniors to join and explore activities at their own comfort level' - PCF).

eligibility_summary: 60+, Singapore Citizen or PR, lives in the centre's boundary; free; no medical diagnosis needed; the centre is a drop-in social space first.
after_joining_person_sees: A weekly and monthly activity schedule on the wall (and by phone/WhatsApp) - exercise classes with fixed times, games, festivals
Interest groups they can pick: music, handicraft, exercises, gardening (Lions Befrienders list)
Befriending: regular home visits or phone calls if they are homebound or alone
Learning: smartphone/tablet classes, language classes, health talks
Ways to give back: volunteer at the centre, deliver meals, read letters, become a Silver Guardian, micro-jobs in the estate
Communal meals and makan sessions, monthly birthdays, festive celebrations and outings
Referrals to care services, grants, Healthier SG plans - the centre is the doorway to the wider system
Their own regular seat: the same class, the same kakis, the same time every week (this is what keeps engagement high)

engagement_mechanics_real.fixed_rituals: Weekly classes at fixed times (taichi 9:15am, line dance 9am) become habits; missed days are noticed by friends and staff
engagement_mechanics_real.social_pressure_kind: Buddy systems, kaki groups, 'kopi kakis' coffee corners
engagement_mechanics_real.recognition: Birthday celebrations, volunteer appreciation, students-to-teachers stories
engagement_mechanics_real.homebound_inclusion: House visits, phone calls, AAS alert monitoring - nobody disappears
engagement_mechanics_real.men_specific: REACH 'Uncle Time' men-only programme; PA brings men in through work/fish/kopi angles
engagement_mechanics_real.intergenerational: Preschool co-location (Kampung Admiralty), youth volunteers, Silver Guardians matched near home

figures_for_realism.pa_wellness: Wellness Programme benefited 500,000+ seniors since 2008; 200+ RCs run Wellness Time

source_urls: moh.gov.sg (Age Well Neighbourhoods, Silver Guardian speech)
